chunks: 3. My father (may Allah have mercy on him) said: Sa'd ibn Abd Allah said: Muhammad ibn al-Husayn ibn Abi al-Khattab said, on the authority of Ahmad ibn Abi Nasr, who said: A group of people came from across the river to Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him) and said to him: We have come to ask you about three matters. If you answer us in them, we will know that you are learned. He said: Ask. They said: Inform us about Allah: Where was He? And how was He? And upon what was His reliance?

He said: Verily, Allah, the Mighty and High, is the Creator of 'how', so He is without 'how'. And He is the Creator of 'where', so He is without 'where'. And His reliance was upon His Omnipotence. They said: We testify that you are learned.

The compiler of this book said: By his statement 'And His reliance was upon His Omnipotence', he means upon His Essence, because Omnipotence is one of the attributes of the Essence of Allah, the Mighty and High.
ai.seo_question: How does Imam al-Rida explain Allah's attributes of place and manner in relation to His essence?
ai.summary: This narration from Shaykh al-Saduq’s *al-Tawhid* highlights the theological debate on divine attributes, specifically addressing whether God's reliance (i'timad) is on His Essence or His attributes. The compiler clarifies that relying on Omnipotence is effectively relying on the Divine Essence, as attributes are inseparable from the Self, reinforcing the Shia doctrine of divine simplicity and transcendence beyond spatial and temporal limitations.

en.sayed-ali-raza-rizvi: 3. My father (RA) said: Sa`d ibn `Abd Allah said: Muhammad ibn al-Husayn ibn Abu al-Khattab said, on the authority of Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Abu Nasr that A group of people came from across the river to see Abu al-Hasan al-Rida (AS) and said: “We have come to ask you three questions. If you can answer all the three question, we will know that you are the Most Learned.” The Imam (AS) said: “Ask.” They said: “Let us know about Allah: Where is He? How is He? And what does He rely upon?”

Hence, he (AS) replied, “Verily, Allah, the Mighty and High, created the quality of `how;’ therefore `how’ does not apply to Hi. He has created space; thus, He is not in need of space. And He relies upon His Omnipotence.” They said: We testify that you are Most Learned One.”

The Compiler of this book (RA) says: The meaning of his statement `He relies upon His Omnipotence’ is that He relies on His Being, because Omnipotence is one of the Essential Attributes of Allah, the Might and High.
